item.title: 1982: Dale Murphy Wins NL MVP, First Braves Player Honored Since Aaron
item.description: Center fielder Dale Murphy wins the National League MVP Award, becoming the first Braves' player to be so honored since Hank Aaron in 1957. Murphy hit .281 with 36 home runs, 109 RBI, 113 runs, and 23 stolen bases. Photo: Whitney & Matt Dellinger from Atlanta, GA, USA (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2022: Mariners Trade Lewis to Diamondbacks for Cooper Hummel
item.description: On November 17, 2022, the Mariners traded Lewis to the Arizona Diamondbacks in exchange for Cooper Hummel. Photo: PaulHamaker Cropped by 佾珜 (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2022: Last Day for Former Club Qualifying Offers to Free Agents
item.description: Last Day for article xx (B) free agents to accept a qualifying offer from a former club (Midnight ET.)

item.title: 2021: Corbin Burnes Wins NL Cy Young Over Zack Wheeler by 10 Votes
item.description: The voting was close in the National League CY Young Award but Corbin Burnes took the honors over Zack Wheeler by 10 votes, while the American League Cy Young award was won by Robbie Ray. Photo: Ian D'Andrea on Flickr (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2021: Marlins Hire Pedrique as Third Base, Infield Coach
item.description: On November 17, 2021, the Marlins hired Pedrique as their third base and infield coach for the 2022 season. Photo: Tnullet (Public domain).

item.title: 2020: Hoyer Named Cubs President of Baseball Operations After Epstein Exit
item.description: On November 17, 2020, the Cubs named Hoyer president of baseball operations, taking over following Epstein's resignation. Photo: Arturo Pardavila III from Hoboken, NJ, USA (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2017: John Hart Steps Down as Braves President Amid MLB Investigation
item.description: John Hart stepped down from his role as Atlanta Braves president of baseball operations, amid an investigation by Major League Baseball into violations related to both the domestic amateur draft and the international signing market.

item.title: 2013: Mary Nesbitt Wisham, American Baseball Player
item.description: Mary Nesbitt Wisham, American baseball player (born 1925)

item.title: 2011: Owners Approve Astros Sale to Jim Crane, Move to AL in 2013
item.description: Major League Baseball owners approve the sale of the Houston Astros to a group led by private equity fund company CEO Jim Crane, with the sale conditional on the team moving to the American League beginning in 2013.

item.title: 2006: Bo Schembechler, 77, Hall of Fame Coach, Former Tigers President
item.description: Bo Schembechler, 77, Hall of Fame college football coach and president of the Detroit Tigers from 1990 to 1992, even though he was widely criticized for the firing of legendary Tigers radio announcer Ernie Harwell.

item.title: 2000: Jason Giambi Named AL MVP Over Frank Thomas, Alex Rodriguez
item.description: Jason Giambi of the Oakland Athletics was named the American League MVP beating out a big lineup of stars like Frank Thomas, Alex Rodriguez and Pedro Martínez. Photo: bryce_edwards (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1998: Glavine Wins Second NL Cy Young in Close Vote Over Hoffman
item.description: Tom Glavine of the Atlanta Braves wins his second National League Cy Young Award in an extremely close vote over two San Diego Padres pitchers: Trevor Hoffman and Kevin Brown. Glavine, who receives 11 first-place votes to Hoffman's 13 (Brown receives the remaining 8), becomes the first National League pitcher since the league instituted its four-vote system in 1970 to win the award despite receiving fewer… Photo: Jeffrey Hayes (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1992: Expansion Draft Held in New York City
item.description: The 1992 Major League Baseball expansion draft was held on November 17, 1992, in New York City.

item.title: 1992: Expansion Draft Stocks Marlins and Rockies With 72 Players
item.description: Major League Baseball holds an expansion draft to stock the rosters of the National League's two new teams, the Florida Marlins and Colorado Rockies. A total of 72 players are chosen. The best picks for Florida are Trevor Hoffman, eventually packaged for Gary Sheffield; Jeff Conine, and Cris Carpenter, later dealt to the Texas Rangers for Robb Nen. Photo: Djh57 (CC BY 3.0).

item.title: 1989: Braves Sign Nick Esasky, 29, After 30-Homer Season in Boston
item.description: The Atlanta Braves sign first baseman Nick Esasky, granted free agency from the Boston Red Sox on November 13. Esasky, 29, is coming off a "career" year in Boston: 30 home runs, 30 doubles and a .500 slugging percentage.

item.title: 1987: George Bell Becomes First Blue Jay to Win AL MVP Over Trammell
item.description: Slugging outfielder George Bell (16 first-place votes, 332 points) becomes the first Toronto Blue Jay to win an American League MVP Award when he defeats Alan Trammell (12 first-place votes, 311 points) of the Detroit Tigers in a two-man race. Bell, 28, led the AL in runs batted in with 134 in 1987. Photo: Robert Taylor from Stirling, ON, Canada (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1983: Willie Wilson, Aikens, Martin, Vida Blue Convicted in Cocaine Case
item.description: Three current Kansas City Royals players (Willie Wilson, Willie Aikens, Jerry Martin) and former Royal Vida Blue are convicted of attempting to purchase cocaine, and sentence to short prison terms. It is a foreshadowing of the coming drug scandal that rocks the sport world throughout the 1980s. Photo: Major League Baseball / Kansas City Royals (Public domain).

item.title: 1979: Dodgers Sign Don Stanhouse, Granted Free Agency by Orioles
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers sign relief pitcher Don Stanhouse, granted free agency from the Baltimore Orioles on November 1.

item.title: 1976: Matthews Signs Five-Year, $1,875,000 Deal With Braves
item.description: During the advent of MLB free agency, Matthews signed a five‐year, $1,875,000 contract with the Braves on November 17, 1976.

item.title: 1971: Vida Blue, 22, Becomes Youngest Player to Win MVP
item.description: At age 22, Oakland Athletics pitcher Vida Blue becomes the youngest player ever to win the Most Valuable Player Award and only the fourth to capture both the Cy Young Award and the MVP in the same season. Photo: William F. Henderson (CC BY 4.0).

item.title: 1969: Cubs Trade Selma to Phillies for Callison and Colton
item.description: Selma was traded to the Philadelphia Phillies on November 17, 1969, with Oscar Gamble for a player to be named later (who became Larry Colton) and Johnny Callison.

item.title: 1969: Phillies Deal Johnny Callison, 30, to Chicago Cubs
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies deal outfielder Johnny Callison, 30, a four-time former NL All-Star, and pitcher Larry Colton ("PTBNL") to the Chicago Cubs for pitcher Dick Selma and outfielder Oscar Gamble. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1968: Earl Hamilton, 77, Pitcher, Later Minor League Owner
item.description: Earl Hamilton, 77, pitcher who appeared in 410 games in MLB between 1911 and 1924, mostly with the St. Louis Browns and Pittsburgh Pirates; later a minor league team owner. Photo: George Grantham Bain Collection (Public domain).

item.title: 1961: Benny Kauff, 71, Federal League Batting and Stolen Base Champ
item.description: Benny Kauff, 71, "the Ty Cobb of the Feds", outfielder who won back-to-back batting (.370 and .342) and stolen base (75 and 55) titles in the 1914–1915 Federal League, then considered an "outlaw" circuit but now recognized as a major league; also played for New York Highlanders of the American League and New York Giants of the National; banned from baseball by Commissioner Kenesaw Mountain Landis after he was tried… Photo: Bain News Service, publisher (Public domain).

item.title: 1958: Mort Cooper, 45, NL MVP Pitcher for Cardinals
item.description: Mort Cooper, 45, pitcher for the St. Louis Cardinals, Boston Braves, New York Giants and Chicago Cubs over 12 seasons from 1938 to 1949; selected to four National League All-Star teams (1942–1943 and 1945–1946); led NL with 22 wins, 10 shutouts and a 1.78 ERA in 1942, earning Most Valuable Player honors, while anchoring Cardinals' pitching staff during three consecutive pennant-winning seasons (1942–1944), when he… Photo: Unknown (Public domain).

item.title: 1949: Fred Hoey, 65, Pioneering Boston Baseball Broadcaster
item.description: Fred Hoey, 65, sportswriter and pioneering baseball broadcaster in Boston; radio voice of both the Braves (1925–1938) and Red Sox (1927–1938). Photo: Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).

item.title: 1947: Browns Trade Vern Stephens to Red Sox for $310,000 and Six Players
item.description: The cash-strapped Browns make the first of two blockbuster trades with the wealthy Boston Red Sox, sending hard-hitting, three-time AL All-Star shortstop Vern Stephens and pitcher Jack Kramer to the Bosox for $310,000 and six players: pitchers Joe Ostrowski, Al Widmar and Jim Wilson, catcher Roy Partee, infielder Eddie Pellagrini and outfielder Pete Layden. Photo: Horner, Carl J (Public domain).

item.title: 1892: National League Owners Shorten 1893 Schedule to 132 Games
item.description: National League magnates conclude a four-day meeting in Chicago where they agree to shorten the 1893 schedule to 132 games and drop the split season schedule (the league's next split season would be 1981). They also pledge to continue to reduce player salaries and other team expenses.

item.title: 1887: Club Owners Recognize Brotherhood of Professional Base-Ball Players
item.description: The club owners officially recognize the Brotherhood of Professional Base-Ball Players by meeting with John Montgomery Ward, Ned Hanlon, and Dan Brouthers. Photo: The Library of Congress (No restrictions).
